title: BE VERY CAREFUL — READ THE FINE PRINT
body:
I purchased a personalised journal from LastingChange for $131, believing I was making a one-off purchase.

What was not made clear to me during the purchase process was that I was apparently also signing up for an ongoing monthly subscription.

The recurring subscription was hidden in the small print rather than being clearly and prominently disclosed.

I certainly did not knowingly agree to a monthly subscription, and I am extremely disappointed that a company selling a product centred around personal wellbeing chooses to use this sort of subscription model.

Whether the terms technically contain the information somewhere in the fine print is beside the point for me. Customers should not have to hunt through small print to discover that a $131 purchase has turned into an ongoing financial commitment of $55 per month.

My advice to anyone considering purchasing: read absolutely everything before entering your payment details and check your account afterwards for recurring charges.

For me, this has completely undermined my trust in the company and turned what should have been a positive purchase into a very sour experience.

body:

Additionally, when I reached out to The Lasting Change’s customer service for a refund due to these discrepancies, their response was less than accommodating. The lack of flexibility and understanding in addressing my concerns as a customer only compounded my dissatisfaction.

While the physical product (a book) associated with this purchase was of decent quality, it did not make up for the shortcomings of the app and the overall customer service experience.

title: Very good tool to stay on track if you’re serious about implementing changes
body:
Once you decide to go ahead with Lasting Change, you have the option to buy either the personalized book only (you get a digital version plus print shipped within a very reasonable delay) or, at a marginally higher, the book plus a 3-month-subscription for the app. 

For me, this implied that, should I decide for the book only and subscribe to the app later, there will be additional cost, so although I am more of a pen-and-paper person, I went ahead with the book/app combo, just in case. The app has a clear structure and seems to be sufficient to stay on track (if you’re serious about change, that is), plus there is an easy option to request additional features (which I didn’t try, but I found it reassuring to know it’s there). Personally, I feel I take things more seriously if I write them down myself, in my own words, with my own hand, so I opted for a paper bullet journal instead - just adds that „contract“ feeling, but again: this is personal preference. If in need for reminders at regular times, the app still is a good option.

Once I was clear about the fact, that I‘d rather track on paper instead of the app, I contacted help@ in order to cancel my subscription to the app at the end of the 3-month-period and got a friendly reply, confirming the cancellation within a quarter of an hour. 

My resume: Lasting Change delivered tools capable of guiding towards as well as tracking changes of behaviours and were easily accessible when needed.

body: … however I am a little disappointed by the nutrition section within the app. Unfortunately it has a very limited amount of meals to choose from and right now I am not quite sure how it is supposed to support healthy eating habits, since there is no “rating” of food quality. Also, I couldn’t find the option to sort of time-stamp the food I ate nor what amount it was. So at the end of the day you just log in you, for example, ate “burger”, “pancakes” and drank coffee, but there is no way to be more precise about it. This “time stamp” is being added automatically to the other tracking sections within the app, like the mood tracker, which I find very helpful as it inspires to reflect more on what exactly drives the mood to change during the day. It’s also nice to have different challenges to choose from. I am still exploring all the options the app has to offer and have not received the Lasting Changes personalised workbook yet, but for now it seems to be a great idea to implement healthy habits into daily life.

title: Misleading, unethical charges – avoid this app
body:
I purchased the Lasting Change physical book over a year ago and downloaded this app only because it was mentioned in the book. I have never consciously activated or used any subscription, yet I was recently charged without warning.

When I contacted support to request a refund for a service I never used, they hid behind a rigid “non-refundable policy.” This feels like a predatory tactic rather than a genuine mental health service. Charging users without clear consent and refusing to refund unintentional renewals is not just bad practice — it’s unethical.

There are far better, more transparent and respectful options for mental wellbeing, like Calm, which actually care about their users. Avoid this app at all costs — it’s built around confusion and zero accountability.

title: Misleading checkout, feels like a scam
body:
I intended to purchase only a book for £62.99. After clicking pay, I was taken to another page that suggested adding a “lifelong subscription” priced at £74.69. The way this was presented made it appear as though this amount was simply the difference between the original price and the higher total — not an additional £74.69 charge.

There was no clear price breakdown, no comparison to other options, and no explicit confirmation step showing the full amount being charged. I wasn’t even clearly told I was making a second purchase. I only realised what had happened after receiving two separate receipt emails.

I contacted the company immediately, explaining that I had no intention of buying lifelong content. Their response was to hide behind Terms and Conditions and refuse any refund, while trying to reframe the situation as “great value.”

The checkout process was misleading, the pricing was unclear, and the lack of transparency feels deceptive. This experience honestly feels like a scam, and the refusal to correct it makes it worse.

I would strongly caution others before purchasing from this company.

title: Lithuanian based company- shady practices
body:
Review: Lasting Change

I’m sharing my experience so others don’t get caught off guard. Lasting Change offers what appears to be a “free month of membership,”  but they hide the fact that they will begin charging you monthly many months afterward. Canceling is extremely difficult because the subscription isn’t set up through any normal or transparent subscription service.

I provided proof that I only purchased their book last January 2025–receipts and all. Despite that, they began charging me around $30 per month starting in September without my knowledge or consent. When I contacted them, they refused to refund any of the charges.

In my experience, this Lithuanian‑based company relies on aggressive advertising (put a LC book in your cart and see how low they will reduce the price if you don’t buy right away) and questionable business practices. I strongly recommend avoiding them so you don’t end up in the same situation.

title: Subscribes you without your knowledge or consent
body: During the checkout process, I explicitly unselected the app option because I was interested in the physical book only. Several weeks later, I was charged $30.99, apparently for a recurring subscription I did not sign up for and which was not clearly outlined during the purchasing process. Customer Service declined to refund me and repeatedly lied that the subscription details are set forth during checkout (so I went back and ran through the process again; they are not) and pointed me to the Terms and Conditions. The fact of an automatic subscription is not even explained in the Terms and Conditions. This company is engaging in consumer fraud to squeeze pennies out of you. 0/10 recommend. Edited pursuant to the developer’s response: the app is not offered as an opt-in during checkout, you are automatically subscribed to it with a purchase of the physical book. And they do not describe the payment terms, though they did add a disclaimer beneath the consent to the terms and conditions in response to my email back-and-forth with them calling out their scam (and then proceeded to lie to me that it had been there all along when I have screenshots contradicting that).

title: Keeps charging after canceling the subscription
body:
I really seriously wish there were more honest reviews on this app when I first made a purchase a few months ago. They seemed like a legit company with lots of reviews — they are not. The “bespoke” book is sloppy in that because the chapters were selected based on what I choose, they don’t share any coherence across. It’s bunch of self help tips that you can easily find online. But i thought that’s okay I’m paying for the service because I know that I wouldn’t look up online to make a book for myself. Well the problem happened when I bought the app which is recommended. First of all, i thought that it wouldn’t make sense to start the app before the book came but the book took a month to get delivered. So I wasted a month of subscription fee, then they charged me again when I haven’t even activated the app so I tried to cancel subscription. IT IS SO HARD TO CANCEL! I emailed the customer service two days after being charged for Feb, saying that I didn’t even activate or sign up in the app. The app is long deleted from my phone but they said “they can’t give me a refund because the service was delivered right” but that they’ve canceled my subscription. Well guess what. I WAS CHARGED AGAIN EVEN AFTER I CANCELED my subscription. I emailed again with the previous email exchange saying that no further payment will be made from them, but the response that  I got was the same response from last month. 1) they’ve delivered the product right 2) THEY CAN’T GIVE ME A REFUND unless it’s a technical fault on their part. 

Charging me after I’ve canceled? I think that’s a technical fault 

and this time, i emailed then within a few hours that they’ve charged me. Whether the service is helpful to you or not would differ by person. But they are being unnecessarily difficult! It’s their fault that that are charging me still. I hope that I can get a refund asap and don’t ever get charged again. Better yet, i hope I never see the name lasting change ever again in my life.

title: Frustrating
body:
First off, I was kind of forced into purchasing a subscription to the app.  I really just wanted the “personalized” book, but they hiked the price of the book if you don’t buy a subscription to the app.

I didn’t use the app at all, I’m sure it works for some people, so I won’t make any comments about the app itself. 

As soon as I purchased the subscription- I made sure I canceled it so that when the (I think) 3 month plan was over - I wouldn’t get charged again.  That wasn’t the case.  I got charged 53.99.  I noticed it the day it was charged, so I immediately emailed customer service to explain everything and ask for a refund.  They got back to me saying they went ahead and canceled my subscription (again, mind you!) but being that the new term already started, they couldn’t reimburse me.  I emailed her back and asked her to reconsider being that it was the same day that they charged me and that I had already cancelled so it was their mistake.  I never got a second reply.

I’m guessing this is how the company makes their money. Such a scam. If it’s such a life changing app, you would think they’d be accommodating to their customers.  Really disappointing.  Maybe this is why people stick with the big companies like Amazon- as much as I hate it, I would have been reimbursed- no questions asked.

Like I told support, I might be missing something but the app is just a place to log stuff. The reminders don’t even tell you what they are for. Just not seeing how this app will help me make a change and create better habits.
